stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group secured a $45 million refinance from City National Bank of Florida for the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, a 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex acquired through a 2024 credit bid. The property has been updated with $3 million in improvements and plans another $3–5 million over the coming year. The asset had lost significant tenant Chewy (100,000 SF) five years prior, and Fortress recently engaged Jamestown for management and leasing.
stories.impact: Refinancing signals stabilization of a distressed South Florida mixed-use asset and reflects lender appetite for value-add office repositioning. Dania Beach office market may see selective demand if Fortress executes leasing against renovation pipeline; however, the property's 100K-SF tenant loss and current economic headwinds in legacy office limit upside for competing multifamily players seeking land or capital in the submarket.

stories.title: Keystone Equities Provides $61M Refi for IOS Repositioning Site in Newark
stories.excerpt: KS Group has secured $60.5 million to refinance a 51-acre industrial site in Newark, N.J., that will be repositioned as an industrial outdoor storage property, Commercial Observer can first report. Keystone Equities provided the debt, structured as a senior bridge loan, marking $660 million in capital the firm has deployed since August 2023, the firm noted in a release. CBRE’s Shlomo Weissberg and Eli Klapper arranged the transaction. Jonathan Zamir, founder and CEO of Keystone Equities, noted in a statement that the site is currently under active environmental remediation and still hadn’t secured a certificate of occupancy before closing, which led to several “traditional lenders” to decline to underwrite the risk associated with the deal. “This was a deal that required real diligence. We dug in, structured around the risks, and found a solution that works for both us and the borrower,” he said. “That’s where Keystone adds value.” Located at 151 Raymond Boulevard in Newark, the industrial site is a former PSEG property that holds proximity to Port Newark-Elizabeth and New York City. The new IOS site will include parking for both trucks and trailers, a container garage for shipping, and electric vehicle and solar charging stations. CBRE noted in recent reports that IOS vacancy in Northern New Jersey stands at 2.5 percent, while rents have grown 123 percent since 2020. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Keystone Equities closed $60.5M senior bridge for 51-acre Newark industrial site repositioning
Property under environmental remediation, lacks certificate of occupancy; traditional lenders declined risk
KS Group converting former PSEG utility property to industrial outdoor storage; bridge structure reflects contamination uncertainty
stories.summary: Keystone Equities provided a $60.5 million senior bridge loan to refinance a 51-acre industrial site at 151 Raymond Boulevard in Newark, New Jersey, being repositioned as an industrial outdoor storage property. The asset is undergoing active environmental remediation and had not obtained a certificate of occupancy at closing, creating risk that traditional lenders declined. Keystone's willingness to structure around environmental and regulatory uncertainty reflects the firm's $660 million deployment since August 2023.
stories.impact: Bridge financing for contaminated industrial sites signals continued capital availability for remediation-dependent projects in the Newark market, but has minimal direct impact on multifamily development. The deal underscores that alternative lenders are filling voids left by traditional underwriters—relevant to multifamily developers seeking non-recourse or acquisition bridge structures in distressed or regulatory-challenged situations.

stories.title: CMBS Special Servicing Rate Dips in July as Office, Lodging Improve
stories.excerpt: The Trepp CMBS special servicing overall rate declined 11 basis points in July to 11.09%, partially reversing the increases of recent months. However, decreases in special servicing rates were not seen across the board in all property types. The improvement was led by office, the largest special servicing category, along with lodging, whose rates fell 53 and 26 bps to 16.58% and 8.63%, respectively. Industrial edged down three bps to 1.34%. That progress outweighed a sharp increase in retail, where a heavy wave of regional-mall loans transferred into special servicing for maturity default, lifting the retail rate 33 bps to 13.28%, Trepp reported Multifamily rose 16 bps to 8.39%, and mixed-use edged up two bps to 11.93%. New transfers to special servicing totaled roughly $1.69 billion across 41 loans and were unusually concentrated in retail, which accounted for about $903.6 million. The flow was dominated by regional malls reaching their balloon maturities. The post CMBS Special Servicing Rate Dips in July as Office, Lodging Improve appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multifamily special servicing rate rose 16 bps to 8.39% in July; overall CMBS rate fell 11 bps to 11.09%
Office and lodging improved (office -53 bps to 16.58%; lodging -26 bps to 8.63%); retail jumped 33 bps to 13.28%
$1.69B in new special servicing transfers; retail (regional malls) accounted for $903.6M, driven by maturity defaults
stories.summary: The Trepp CMBS special servicing rate fell 11 basis points in July to 11.09%, led by improvements in office (-53 bps to 16.58%) and lodging (-26 bps to 8.63%). However, multifamily rose 16 basis points to 8.39%, while retail surged 33 bps to 13.28%, driven by $903.6 million in regional mall loans hitting balloon maturity. Total new special servicing transfers reached $1.69 billion across 41 loans.
stories.impact: Rising multifamily special servicing signals stress in select multifamily CMBS pools—likely concentrated in older, high-leverage deals originated 2019–2021 with near-term maturities. While office pain masks multifamily's modest deterioration, the 16 bp uptick warrants monitoring of regional-specific CMBS maturity walls and potential distressed sale opportunities in markets with high CMBS-backed inventory, particularly secondary metros. Conversely, it signals tightening underwriting for new construction debt.

stories.title: Return to Lender: Week of August 13, 2026
stories.excerpt: An out-of-state hedge fund has won an auction to acquire the entirety of Spirit Airlines’ former headquarters in South Florida with a $93.25-million cash bid. The South Florida Business Journal reported that the now-defunct carrier named DPC HoldCo LLC, an affiliate of Boston-based Hill City Capital, as the successful bidder in a notice of auction results. Hill City was also the stalking horse bidder in the auction, which was brokered by Savills Eastdil Secured. A downtown San Antonio office building, anchored by La Panaderia Bakery & Café on the ground floor, has sold in a distressed sale. The Vogue Building at 600 Navarro St. traded in an Aug. 5 foreclosure auction for about $5.2 million, the San Antonio Business Journal reported. Ownership entity Vogue SATX LLC, connected to local investor Dr. Sanjay Misra, defaulted on a $6 million loan drawn up by Blue Sky Bank. The bank took control of the property, which was last appraised at $6 million, per the Bexar Central Appraisal District. U.S. National Bank Association, the lender for Denver’s tallest tower, has requested a receiver for the property after ownership defaulted on an approximately $130-million loan, reported the Denver Business Journal. Republic Plaza, at 370 17th St., is owned by Brookfield Properties and insurer MetLife. The retail space at Brightline MiamiCentral Station could be seized in a $65-million foreclosure lawsuit, according to the Orlando Business Journal. U.S. Bank, acting as administrative agent for two groups of lenders, filed a foreclosure complaint July 30 against Brightline Investment Holdings and DTS DT Retail LLC, along with property manager FECI Realty. The roughly 124,000 square feet of retail at 600 N.W. 1st Ave. is owned by DTS DT Retail, which is a subsidiary of Brightline Investment Holdings. Buffalo Business First reported that a New York City developer is now facing foreclosure proceedings against a second large apartment community in Amherst. Acres Loan Origination

stories.title: Florida People & Companies, August 14, 2026
stories.excerpt: West Palm Beach, Fla. – PTM Partners and Hernandez Development & Construction acquired an 8.13-acre development site at 8530 Belvedere Road in West Palm Beach, Florida for $11.5 million. The site will be developed as Palm Beach Commerce Center, a 93,556-square-foot Class A industrial facility with 32-foot clear heights, 22 dock doors and more than 180 feet of building depth. Previously approved for retail, gas station, and daycare uses, the site is being repositioned to address the continued demand for logistics and distribution space in Palm Beach County.  Former Miami Beach City Manager Jimmy Morales, has been hired by Bilzin Sumberg, as Special Counsel. Morales joins the firm’s Land Development & Government Relations Group. His arrival strengthens Bilzin Sumberg’s ability to serve clients navigating consequential transactions, strategic initiatives, government matters, regulatory challenges and opportunities for growth. Wood Partners hired Micah Conn as Managing Director of the firm’s South Florida office. Conn will oversee all aspects of development across the region, including origination, entitlements, design, capitalization and construction management. Conn has more than 20 years of experience in multifamily and mixed-use development. Before joining Wood Partners, he served as senior vice president of development at AvalonBay Communities. Miami-based Gencom Real Estate will be led by Donald McGregor, who has been promoted to President of Gencom Real Estate. In this leadership role, he will oversee the execution of the firm’s strategies across development, construction, and asset management, ensuring disciplined delivery from acquisition through stabilization and exit, while creating long-term value across the portfolio. stories.title: Jackson-Shaw Starts Work on 900K-SF Denton Industrial Project
stories.excerpt: Jackson-Shaw broke ground on Horizon 35, a master-planned business park at the northeast corner of Interstate 35 and Loop 288 in Denton, Texas. Phase I will deliver 543,550 square feet across three rear-load buildings and is now pre-leasing for delivery in the third quarter of 2027. At full buildout, the development will total more than 900,000 square feet and accommodate a range of tenant sizes. A future Phase II offers up to 400,000 square feet for build-to-suit. Along the I-35 corridor, Horizon 35 offers frontage and access to Interstate 35, Loop 288, and U.S. Highway 77. Phase I includes Building 1 at 147,390 square feet, Building 2 at 145,920 square feet, and Building 3 at 250,240 square feet. ARCO/Murray is serving as the design-builder. The Stream Realty Partners leasing team for Horizon 35 includes Forrest Cook, Mac Hall and Connor Land. The post Jackson-Shaw Starts Work on 900K-SF Denton Industrial Project appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Jackson-Shaw commenced construction on Horizon 35, a master-planned 900,000-square-foot industrial business park at the northeast corner of I-35 and Loop 288 in Denton, Texas. Phase I will deliver 543,550 square feet across three rear-load buildings in Q3 2027, with Phase II offering up to 400,000 square feet for build-to-suit. stories.impact: Large-scale industrial pipeline in the Denton I-35 corridor signals ongoing supply growth in a key Dallas metro logistics submarket, which may absorb tenants and capital that could have flowed to adjacent Dallas proper. Denton's industrial growth reflects broader North Texas warehouse expansion, but has minimal direct multifamily demand effect unless logistics job creation in the submarket drives worker housing migration into adjacent residential markets (Frisco, Plano, Carrollton). Developers should monitor Denton rent growth and demographic trends to gauge secondary housing demand.

stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Relocates to 5K SF at GFP’s 515 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Zimmet Law Group is relocating its practice inside Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet signed a 5,476-square-foot lease for a newly completed space inside GFP Real Estate’s 515 Madison Avenue, also known as the DuMont Building. Located at the corner of East 53rd Street, the 42-story office tower is just one block south of Zimmet’s current abode in RFR Holding’s 477 Madison Avenue. Zimmet’s practice areas range widely, from matrimonial and family law to real estate matters. The law firm was represented by Savitt Partners’ Elliot Zelinger, while GFP’s Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone negotiated in-house for the landlord. Zelinger did not respond to a request for comment. Asking rent for the nearly 10-year lease term was not disclosed, but office asking rents in Midtown averaged $88.50 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield data. Zimmet is expected to take occupancy at 515 Madison later this year, according to GFP, following the completion of its new space. Zimmet’s office did not respond to a request for comment on the relocation. Earlier this year, GFP took full ownership of the 350,000-square-foot Class A tower after securing an $86.5 million refinancing deal with Apple Bank, which enabled the buyout of ATCO Properties & Management’s remaining 40 percent stake in the property. By late February, the landlord had secured 12,000 square feet of new leasing activity, Commercial Observer reported. GFP announced another 9,000 square feet of deals in late July, including leases for investment firm T7 Capital, aesthetic training provider Innovation Training Specialist and Widowski Law Group. Other tenants at 515 Madison include alternative asset manager Whitebox and therapy provider Manhattan Psychiatry Group. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group leased 5,476 square feet of newly completed office space at GFP Real Estate's 515 Madison Avenue (DuMont Building) in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from RFR's 477 Madison one block south. The nearly 10-year lease was signed at asking rents near Midtown's Q2 2026 average of $88.50 per square foot, with occupancy expected later in 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily development; this is a small Manhattan office renewal in a premium submarket. No signal of broad office-to-residential conversion, major tenant flight, or demand deterioration in Midtown. The lease represents localized Plaza District office stability and GFP's ability to lease newly built space, but does not influence multifamily acquisition, construction, or financing strategy.

stories.title: Sixth Street Acquires Iconic Pier House Hotel in Key West for $190M
stories.excerpt: An iconic luxury hotel in Key West, Fla., is changing hands. Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital have acquired Pier House, a longstanding 142-room oceanfront resort in downtown Key West, from Braemar Hotels & Resorts in a $190 million deal, according to a release from Sixth Street. Starwood Property Trust provided the debt financing, the amount of which has not been disclosed, while the Plasencia Group advised Braemar Hotels & Resorts on the sale. Aman Gupta, principal at Sixth Street, noted in a statement that Pier House has access to a private beach and includes unobstructed sunset views for its guests while also being in the heart of Downtown Key West. “This investment reflects Sixth Street’s commitment to identifying high-quality hospitality assets where we can drive long-term value,” said Gupta. Located at 1 Duval Street, Pier Street sits on five acres of beachfront land along the famous Duval Street, a top tourist destination and walkable retail and entertainment thoroughfare. The resort first opened in 1967 and had been owned by Braemar Hotels & Resorts since 2014. On-site amenities include two oceanfront restaurants, a spa, a fitness center, an oceanfront pool and 3,000 square feet of event space. “We believe Pier House represents an opportunity to acquire a historic luxury resort in one of the country’s most supply-constrained and sought-after tropical leisure markets,” said Gupta. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital acquired Pier House, 142-room Key West oceanfront resort, for $190M

stories.summary: Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital acquired Pier House Resort and Spa, a 142-room luxury oceanfront hotel in downtown Key West, from Braemar Hotels & Resorts for $190 million. Located on five acres at 1 Duval Street with private beach access and sunset views, Starwood Property Trust provided debt financing. The investors cited the property's premium beachfront location and tourism destination positioning as drivers of long-term value.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development strategy. Key West hospitality remains a specialized, supply-constrained asset class with minimal overlap with residential development. However, the deal signals continued PE and debt appetite for premium hospitality in constrained coastal markets, reflecting broader confidence in post-pandemic leisure travel and suggests capital may be flowing away from secondary-market multifamily toward trophy hospitality assets.

stories.title: Heights Advisors Files Plans to Build 606 Affordable Units in the Bronx
stories.excerpt: Heights Advisors, a Brooklyn-based development and investment firm led by founder and president Rachel Foster, is planning to bring 606 affordable housing units to the Bronx’s Soundview neighborhood. The firm filed a land use application Wednesday with the New York City Department of City Planning requesting a zoning amendment and a special permit to build a 21-story mixed-use building with 606 units at 945 White Plains Road. The filing initiates a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), which typically takes about seven months of public review of the proposed zoning changes, and includes formal hearings before a final vote by the City Council and City Planning Commission. If approved, Heights Advisors’ proposed project would span 515,063 square feet and include 503,095 square feet of residential space and 11,968 square feet of commercial space, the application notes. The Brooklyn developer is seeking construction financing under the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development’s New Construction Finance Program, which provides funding for the construction of 100 percent affordable multifamily rental projects, according to the filing. Of Heights Advisors’ 606 planned units, approximately 152 are set to be affordable. It’s unclear whether Heights Advisors, which is the ground lessee of 945 White Plains Road on a 99-year ground lease, plans to demolish the current retail property on the site, which is home to a Modell’s Sporting Goods and GameStop. Heights Advisors did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Other residential developments planned for the Bronx include a 228-unit affordable senior housing development at 3728 Park Avenue, as well as a pair of 99-unit residential buildings at 761-769 East Tremont Avenue. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Heights Advisors filed ULURP for 606 affordable units in 21-story building at 945 White Plains Road, Bronx Soundview

stories.summary: Heights Advisors, a Brooklyn-based developer, filed a land use application with NYC Department of City Planning for a 21-story mixed-use building with 606 affordable housing units at 945 White Plains Road in the Bronx's Soundview neighborhood. The 515,063-square-foot project includes 503,095 square feet of residential space and 11,968 square feet of commercial space, and the developer is seeking construction financing through the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development's New Construction Finance Program. The Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) typically takes approximately seven months.
stories.impact: Material supply signal for East Bronx multifamily market: 606 units of subsidized affordable housing will compete directly with market-rate and workforce housing in the Soundview submarket, likely depressing rents for unsubsidized product and limiting pricing power for nearby private developers. The reliance on HPD financing and lengthy ULURP timeline suggests this project will not deliver before 2028–2029, creating a multi-year window for competitive market-rate development. Developers targeting the Bronx should assess whether Soundview is saturating with affordable-only pipelines and consider adjacent neighborhoods (Pelham Bay, Throggs Neck) for market-rate multifamily opportunities.
